 FILE PHOTO: An Anthropic logo is displayed at Moscone Center during the Dreamforce 2026 technology summit in San Francisco, California, US, September 17, 2026. REUTERS/Carlos Barria/File Photo 
 Nov 3 (Reuters) - AI ⁠giant Anthropic, which filed for a US ⁠IPO last week, is expected to include ‌an Australian retail share offer in its prospectusto befiledwith the country's corporate regulator, the Commonwealth Bank of Australia's ​broking unit said on Tuesday.
 Here ⁠are some details:
 • Commonwealth ⁠Securities(CommSec)said it will act as lead Australian retail broker ⁠forAnthropic's ‌Australian retail offer, if the IPO proceeds
 • Anthropic will not be applying ⁠for listing on the Australian Securities Exchange, ​CommSec added
 • ‌The Claude maker, which is expected to go ⁠public ​before Thanksgiving, will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol "ANT" after the IPO closes
 • Anthropic's listing ⁠comes as investors evaluate whether ​AI-driven capital expenditure will deliver returns to justify sky-high valuations
 • Some current and prospective investors are weighing ⁠a $1.5 trillion valuation, down from roughly $2 trillion, after the startup disclosed financial details at a recent investor event, Reuters has reported
 • The company expects ​to incur nearly half ⁠of the $895.4 billion in spending commitments related to AI ​infrastructure buildoutsbefore December 31, 2030, ‌adding to investors' concerns ​ahead of the IPO
 (Reporting by Keshav Singh Chundawat in Bengaluru; Editing by Rashmi Aich)
